title: Migration's zero gaps: a pulsing 'live' tally on 0 and a header-only table
body:
## Summary
GAPS is empty, and the Migration tab draws that as live work waiting on a person (an amber tally with a pulsing gold dot on the number 0) above a gaps table that has a header row and no body rows.

## Description
migrationMap.ts:27 declares `GAPS: readonly Gap[] = []` (every gap from the 2026-09-29 measurement is closed). KitView.tsx:62 still passes `tally: { value: GAPS.length, tone: "amber" }`. In the Almanac world Tally maps amber to `k-tally k-tally--live` (components/ui/signal/Tally.tsx ALMANAC_TONE), which kit.css:199-203 draws as a gold border plus a dot animated by `k-tw 2.4s infinite`. Tally.tsx's own doc says amber means "live, or waiting on a person". So the tab rail permanently signals pending work on a count of zero. Inside the tab, Migration.tsx:47-56 hands `ranked` (empty) to DataTable. Doc.tsx:55-78 has no empty branch, so the result is a five-column header ('Gap, Missing part, Shape, First hit, Modules') with nothing under it. The page breaks its own rule: catalog.ts:457 WHEN_TO_USE says 'An empty list -> Ghost ... never "nothing here yet"', and Law renders that rule one tab to the left. The 'Missing' column (Migration.tsx:35-39) is also empty in all 10 MODULES rows.

## Flow
- Open /kit -> the Migration tab's '0' pulses gold on every page load
- Open #migration -> the 'What the kit does not have' table is a header with no body

## Expected impact
The only live-styled signal on the page stops lying, and the reference page for builders shows the empty-list shape it tells them to use.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an amber 'live' tally should mean something is waiting; on /kit it shows 0 and still pulses
Before: 1 live-toned tally on value 0 (KitView.tsx:62). Gaps table renders 1 header row + 0 body rows (Migration.tsx:47). 0 Ghost on the route's empty branch
After: tally tone neutral when GAPS.length === 0. A <Ghost shape="row" label="no gaps"> in place of the empty DataTable
Method: probe - source read of KitView.tsx/Migration.tsx plus the Tally/kit.css mapping; GAPS.length measured = 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/kit/migrationMap.ts:27 (GAPS = []); app/kit/KitView.tsx:62 (tone: "amber"); components/ui/signal/Tally.tsx ALMANAC_TONE amber -> 'k-tally k-tally--live'; components/kit/kit.css:199-203 (.k-tally--live::before animation k-tw infinite); app/kit/Migration.tsx:47-56 (DataTable rows=ranked, no empty branch); components/kit/Doc.tsx:55-78 (DataTable has no empty state); app/kit/catalog.ts:457 (WHEN_TO_USE: empty list -> Ghost)
verify: New tests/golden-path/kit-migration-empty.probe.spec.ts: (1) stripComments(app/kit/KitView.tsx) must not contain the literal `tone: "amber"` unconditionally on the migration tab. Assert the migration tally's tone expression references GAPS.length (regex /GAPS\.length\s*\?\s*"amber"/ or equivalent). (2) stripComments(app/kit/Migration.tsx) contains `<Ghost` and a `length === 0` / `length ?` guard around the gaps DataTable. Red on HEAD, green after. Then npm run typecheck && npm run check:narration (the Ghost label is sr-only, not narration).

title: Part-group jump links break /kit addressability: reload lands on Identity
body:
## Summary
The Parts tab's group jump links rewrite the URL hash to #g-<group>, a hash KitView does not recognise. Reloading or sharing that URL opens the Identity tab, and the anchor it names is not in the DOM.

## Description
KitView.tsx:30 says 'A module is addressable: /kit#parts opens the specimen sheet', and its hash reader (KitView.tsx:31-39) accepts only the four MODULES ids. Parts.tsx:1070-1073 renders `<a href={`#g-${g.id}`}>` for each of the 29 KIT_GROUPS. Clicking one sets location.hash to e.g. `#g-forms`. The hashchange handler runs, finds no module, and leaves the tab alone, so the jump works the first time. The URL now names a part group, not a module. On reload, useState('identity') (KitView.tsx:28) runs and fromHash rejects 'g-forms', so Identity renders. The browser's anchor scroll finds no #g-forms because Parts is unmounted. The link a builder copies to share 'the Forms specimens' opens a different tab at the top of the page.

## Flow
- /kit#parts -> click 'Forms' in the jump nav -> URL is /kit#g-forms
- Reload (or paste the URL in a new tab) -> Identity tab, top of page, no Forms section anywhere

## Expected impact
Every part group on the specimen sheet becomes a working deep link, which is what a reference page is used for.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a copied /kit#g-forms link should open the Forms specimens
Before: 29 jump-link hashes (KIT_GROUPS.length) resolve to the Identity tab on load. 0 of 29 deep-link correctly
After: 29 of 29 open the Parts tab and scroll to their group
Method: probe - source read of KitView.tsx:28-44 and Parts.tsx:1070-1076. The hash->module mapping is a pure function a node probe can assert
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/kit/KitView.tsx:30-39 (fromHash accepts MODULES only); app/kit/KitView.tsx:28 (initial 'identity'); app/kit/Parts.tsx:1070-1073 (href=#g-${g.id}); app/kit/Parts.tsx:1076 (id=g-${g.id}, only mounted on the parts tab)
verify: Add a pure `kitModuleForHash(hash: string): "identity"|"law"|"parts"|"migration"|null` to app/kit/catalog.ts (plain data file, node-importable): a module id maps to itself, and `g-<id>` maps to 'parts' when <id> is a KIT_GROUPS id. Anything else maps to null. KitView's fromHash uses it, and after setTab('parts') for a g- hash it scrolls `document.getElementById(h)` into view on the next frame. New tests/golden-path/kit-hash.probe.spec.ts imports it and asserts ('parts')->'parts', ('g-forms')->'parts', ('g-nope')->null, ('')->null, plus a source ratchet that stripComments(KitView.tsx) calls kitModuleForHash. Red on HEAD (export absent), green after. npm run typecheck.

title: Kit TabRail controls no panel: no tabpanel, no aria-controls (siblings do)
body:
## Summary
The /kit tab rail is role=tablist/tab, but the content it switches is a bare div with no tabpanel role and no aria-controls link. The other TabRail hosts in the app wire both.

## Description
KitView.tsx:54-68 passes four tabs with no `panelId` and renders `{tab === 'identity' && <Identity/>}` etc. directly. TabRail forwards `panelId` to `aria-controls` (components/ui/signal/TabRail.tsx TabDef.panelId -> aria-controls). LibraryView.tsx:83/102/116 pass `panelId: "library-panel"` and render `<section id="library-panel" role="tabpanel">` (:123). PlaygroundView.tsx:101-119 and :136 do the same, and so does ScriptStep.tsx:401/:410. /kit is the page that teaches builders how to use TabRail, and it is the only Almanac-world host that skips the panel half of the pattern. A screen reader user hears 'tab, selected, 2 of 4' with no 'controls' relation and no panel landmark to jump to.

## Flow
- SR user on /kit tabs to 'Parts' and presses Enter -> no tabpanel exists to move to. The rail announces no controls relation

## Expected impact
The reference host of TabRail models the full ARIA tabs pattern its siblings already follow.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an AT user can move from a selected tab to the panel it controls
Before: 0 of 4 kit tabs carry aria-controls; 0 role=tabpanel on the route. Siblings: LibraryView 3/3, PlaygroundView 3/3, ScriptStep wired
After: 4 of 4 tabs carry panelId 'kit-panel'. 1 `<div id="kit-panel" role="tabpanel" aria-label={tab}>` wraps the module
Method: probe - grep of panelId/role="tabpanel" across TabRail hosts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/kit/KitView.tsx:54-68 (no panelId, no tabpanel); app/library/LibraryView.tsx:83,102,116,123; app/playground/PlaygroundView.tsx:101,110,119,136; app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:401,410; components/ui/signal/TabRail.tsx (panelId -> aria-controls)
verify: Source ratchet (append to tests/golden-path/kit-hash.probe.spec.ts, or a new kit-tabpanel probe): stripComments(app/kit/KitView.tsx) contains role="tabpanel" exactly once and `panelId:` 4 times (or once via a shared spread), and the tabpanel element's id equals the panelId value. Red on HEAD (0 / 0), green after. npm run typecheck.

title: Law rule 12 says vellum >= 11:1; on field it is 10.7 and its gate cannot fail
body:
## Summary
Law rule 12 says white and vellum are both 11:1 or better, and names 'the /kit contrast table' as the gate that holds it. Vellum on --al-field measures 10.68:1, and that table prints the cell as '10.7 AAA' unflagged, because it only flags text tokens graded 'fails' (<3:1).

## Description
catalog.ts:445: `{ rule: "One muting level: white, then vellum, both 11:1 or better.", gate: "/kit contrast table, computed from WORLD_ALMANAC" }`. Token values (components/ui/tokens.ts:241,244): --al-field #121C44, --al-vellum #D6D0BE. contrast.ts's own WCAG formula gives vellum 11.93 on night, 12.76 on deep, 10.68 on field. Identity.tsx:144 adds `kr-rowflag` only when `t === "fails"`, so no ratio between 3 and 11 can ever flag in the Palette table. The sibling TextOnHue table one heading below flags `r < 7` (Identity.tsx:161). The same flag colour means two different thresholds on one page, and neither is the rule's 11. --al-field is the 'raised panel' ground (catalog.ts:367: 'panels, table heads'), so vellum on field is the secondary text in every DataTable header the kit draws. The rule is false today, and the gate it cites cannot catch it.

## Flow
- /kit#identity -> Law tab rule 12 says 11:1 -> Identity palette row --al-vellum, 'On field' column prints 10.7 AAA, unflagged

## Expected impact
Either the rule or the token becomes true, and the Palette table can flag a breach of the page's own stated floor.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a rule on the Law tab is true of the tokens it governs, and its cited gate can fail
Before: vellum/field = 10.68:1 vs stated floor 11. 0 cells flagged. Flag thresholds on one page: <3 (Palette) and <7 (TextOnHue)
After: 1 decision: retune --al-vellum (e.g. a lighter vellum that clears 11 on field) or restate the floor at the measured value. Plus 1 flag threshold for text tokens, read from the rule
Method: probe - computed with contrast.ts's formula over WORLD_ALMANAC (node one-liner, same luminance/contrast code)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/kit/catalog.ts:445 (rule 12 + gate); components/ui/tokens.ts:241 (--al-field #121C44), :244 (--al-vellum #D6D0BE); computed vellum on night/deep/field = 11.93 / 12.76 / 10.68; app/kit/Identity.tsx:144 (flag only on 'fails'); app/kit/Identity.tsx:161 (flag on r < 7)
verify: Extend tests/golden-path/kit-catalog.probe.spec.ts: for --al-white and --al-vellum, contrast(resolve(token), resolve(g)) >= the floor stated in RULES (parse the number from the rule text, or export it as a constant) for g in night/deep/field. Red on HEAD (10.68 < 11), green after the director picks retune vs restate. Identity.tsx's ratioCell then flags text tokens below that same constant.

title: Specimen files hand-roll Button and Chip markup the kit exports (12 sites)
body:
## Summary
The specimen sheet that enforces 'a local duplicate of a kit part is a finding' writes raw `k-btn` buttons and `k-chip` spans in 12 places, where the kit's own `<Button>`, `<Chip>` and `<Chips>` produce the same class strings.

## Description
catalog.ts:449 (Law rule 16): 'A local duplicate of a kit part is a finding.' components/kit/index.ts:3 says the same. PartsWorkbench.tsx:174-176, 238 and 254 render `<button type="button" className="k-btn k-btn--line k-btn--sm">`, which is exactly what `<Button variant="ghost" size="sm">` renders in the Almanac world (components/ui/Primitives.tsx:51-54 maps ghost->line). GrowG3Demos.tsx:218, 219, 286 and 448 render `<span className="k-chip">`, which is what `<Chip>` renders with no name or tone (components/kit/Chip.tsx:18). GrowG3Demos.tsx:217, 282 and 446 render `<div className="k-chips">`, which is `<Chips>` (Chip.tsx:31-32). Today the swap changes no pixels. The value is that the page stops modelling the copy-the-class shortcut, and a future change to Button/Chip (a focus ring, a token) reaches these specimens too.

## Flow
- Read PartsWorkbench.tsx / GrowG3Demos.tsx as a builder -> the reference page shows raw k-btn markup beside the <Button> specimen

## Expected impact
The reference page obeys its own rule 16, and the specimens track the parts they surround.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the kit's reference page uses the kit's parts
Before: 12 hand-rolled sites in app/kit (5 k-btn buttons, 4 k-chip spans, 3 k-chips divs)
After: 0 hand-rolled sites. Same rendered class strings, so no visual diff
Method: probe - grep count over app/kit/*.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep 'className="k-btn' app/kit -> PartsWorkbench.tsx:174,175,176,238,254; grep 'className="k-chip"' -> GrowG3Demos.tsx:218,219,286,448; grep 'className="k-chips"' -> GrowG3Demos.tsx:217,282,446; components/ui/Primitives.tsx:51-54; components/kit/Chip.tsx:18,31-32; app/kit/catalog.ts:449
verify: Add to tests/golden-path/kit-catalog.probe.spec.ts: over app/kit/*.tsx (stripComments), count /className="k-btn\b/ + /className="k-chips?"/ and expect 0. Red on HEAD (12), green after swapping to <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">, <Chip>, <Chips> imported from @/components/kit (style props such as marginBottom move to a wrapper or stay on a parent div). npm run typecheck.

lens_checked.visual-craft: read kit-route.css in full against kit.css tokens (all colours var(--al-*)/--k-*). grep of raw k-btn/k-chip spellings in app/kit. Computed WORLD_ALMANAC text-token contrast on night/deep/field (gold 8.25-9.86, white 14.2-16.95, vellum 10.68-12.76, ald-t 7.45-8.90, ant-t 7.34-8.76)
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: KitView hash handling vs Parts jump nav; ConfirmDemo/SheetDemo/ToastDemo open-close paths; ContextMenu/FolderTree demos
lens_checked.state-coverage: Migration (GAPS = [] -> header-only table, live tally). Parts DEMOS Record<PartName> coverage (typecheck-held). TypeSpec measured px fallback '—' before fonts.ready. No fetching on the route (static fixtures only)
lens_checked.copy-auditor: every RULES/WHEN_TO_USE row against the code it cites. KitView header comment names 'migration.ts' where the file is migrationMap.ts (comment only, not emitted). Identity Stats figures checked against globals.css --text-content 1.125rem / --text-label 1rem
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: TabRail panel wiring vs Library/Playground/Script hosts. Construction/figs svg role=img + aria-label present. Palette swatches aria-hidden. Spec sections are named regions (~90 region landmarks via section[aria-label]), noted, not filed. Global :focus-visible in kit.css:85 covers .kr-jump links

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: desktop reference page. kit-route.css has one 860px breakpoint for the construction grid and auto-fill grids elsewhere; no narrow-first intent
